name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 457 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% more than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 457 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Militant attacks continue in Manipur, with villagers shot while collecting firewood and a pre-dawn arson that gutted a hamlet, prompting security forces to boost operations and a statewide manhunt. Protesters have placed bodies of killed civilians outside the chief minister's residence, while the Joint Tribes Council has called for a security review after the attacks. In northern Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness, and buses bound for Kashmir were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled as terrorists. A cabinet expansion is planned after the lieutenant governor returns to the region. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantangrep fortsetter i Manipur, med landsbyboere skutt mens de samlet vedfyr og en brann før daggry som ødela en landsby, noe som førte til at sikkerhetsstyrkene økte operasjonene og satte i gang en landsomfattende jakt. Demonstranter har plassert likene til drepte sivile utenfor statsministerens residens, mens Joint Tribes Council har krevd en sikkerhetsgjennomgang etter angrepene. I Nord-Kashmir har kommandanten for Northern Army gjennomgått sikkerhet og operasjonell beredskap, og busser på vei til Kashmir ble angrepet i Punjab og Haryana, med passasjerer merket som terrorister. En kabinettutvidelse er planlagt etter at visepresidenten vender tilbake til regionen. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
